channel.title: Runix Blog
channel.description: Engineering notes on LLM gateways, reliability, cost control and data pipelines, from the team building Runix.

item.title: How long should an LLM request be allowed to take?
item.description: Standard HTTP timeout advice is wrong for model traffic. Which timeout to set, where each one belongs, and why stacked timeouts cause the outage.

item.title: What to settle before an LLM feature carries real traffic
item.description: Twelve decisions that are cheap before launch and expensive after: cost ceilings, timeouts, failover, what you log, and how you roll back.

item.title: Your model id has an expiry date
item.description: Providers retire model versions on a published schedule. If the id is a string literal in your code, their calendar is your deploy calendar.

item.title: "OpenAI-compatible" is a surface, not a contract
item.description: Compatibility claims cover the endpoint shape, rarely the details that break you: ignored parameters, missing usage, streaming that ends wrong. How to test one.

item.title: How to tell whether a model change made things worse
item.description: Output varies run to run, so a quality regression does not announce itself. Four signals that move before anyone files a ticket.

item.title: Migrating to a gateway without a maintenance window
item.description: Shadow, then a percentage, then a cutover you can reverse in one config change — and the three things about LLM traffic the usual playbook does not cover.

item.title: Comic Drama vs Webtoon vs Motion Comic, Explained
item.description: Three overlapping formats for drawn stories: how webtoons, motion comics and comic dramas differ in production, distribution and audience — and which to make.

item.title: How to Make a Comic Drama with AI: Script to Screen
item.description: The full AI comic drama production line: script and characters, storyboards, styled panels, motion, voice and publishing — and where tools still fall short.

item.title: LLM Router vs LLM Gateway: What's the Difference?
item.description: The two names describe overlapping tools. What routing and gateway features actually do, when the difference matters, and how to choose on capabilities.

item.title: OpenRouter Alternatives: A Buyer's Checklist
item.description: Evaluating LLM gateways beyond routing: the contract, data, failover and cost-attribution questions that decide whether a gateway survives procurement.

item.title: What Is an LLM Gateway? A Plain Definition
item.description: An LLM gateway is a control plane between your application and model providers. What it does, what it does not do, and when a team actually needs one.

item.title: Surviving LLM Rate Limits: 429s, Budgets and Queues
item.description: Why provider rate limits bite in bursts, how RPM, TPM and concurrency interact, and the queueing and backoff patterns that keep throughput stable under 429s.

item.title: Streaming LLM Responses Without Breaking Failover
item.description: Once tokens have reached the user, failover stops being free. Mid-stream failure modes, what a proxy must preserve, and how to degrade without duplicating text.

item.title: What to Log for LLM Traffic, and What Not To
item.description: Status codes and latency miss the failures that matter for LLM traffic. The signals worth recording, the fields to redact, and the alerts worth waking up for.

item.title: LLM Provider Keys: Scope, Rotation and Blast Radius
item.description: Provider keys spread through repos, CI and notebooks. How to scope and rotate them, and why a compromised LLM key is a billing incident as well as a data one.

item.title: Per-Team LLM Cost Attribution That Survives Audit
item.description: Provider invoices arrive as one number. How to attach cost to a team, feature and request at call time, and why reconstructing it later never works.

item.title: Prompt Caching: When It Pays and When It Bites
item.description: How provider-side prompt caching works, the prefix rule that decides whether you get hits, and the cases where caching quietly changes behaviour.

item.title: 12 Data Questions to Ask an AI Vendor
item.description: The data-handling questions that decide an AI procurement review, what a good answer sounds like, and which vague replies should stop the process.

item.title: Build or Buy an LLM Gateway: An Honest Comparison
item.description: The first version of a gateway is a weekend. The parts that take a year are retry budgets, streaming failover, cost accounting and being on call for all of it.

item.title: LLM Cost Control: Tokens, Caching and Budgets
item.description: Token pricing asymmetry, prompt caching, model routing, budgets and kill switches — and the waste patterns that quietly inflate an LLM bill.

item.title: Building AI Data Pipelines: Raw to Model-Ready
item.description: A stage-by-stage guide to AI data pipelines: ingestion, cleaning, deduplication, LLM-powered extraction, PII masking and quality scoring.

item.title: Model Failover for Production LLM Traffic
item.description: Keeping LLM-backed products up when providers degrade: failure taxonomy, retry budgets, circuit breakers, failover trade-offs and degradation tiers.

item.title: Choosing an LLM Gateway: 7 Things That Matter
item.description: How to evaluate an LLM gateway: API compatibility, failover behaviour, rate limits, cost tracking, observability, security and operational burden.

item.title: Introducing Runix
item.description: Why we are building an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, managed data pipelines and ready-to-deploy solutions — and what comes next.
